long_biography.plain_text:
Pruitt prepared for leadership in a healthcare business that began as his father's northeast Georgia pharmacy and developed into a regional care organization. He studied economics at the University of the South, then earned graduate degrees in business and health administration from Georgia State. That training equipped him to combine family-company stewardship with the operational demands of senior care.

As chairman and chief executive, he continued PruittHealth's expansion beyond nursing centres into rehabilitation, home health, hospice, senior living, pharmacy and managed care. His influence also extended into public policy. He chaired the American Health Care Association, launched a national quality initiative and helped establish shared performance measures for post-acute providers. A federal commission appointment placed him among the advisers considering a coordinated long-term-care system for older adults and people with disabilities.
